refined_summary: Search discovery sharpens the cognition-to-capital-to-failure arc. AbbVie announced the Stemcentrx acquisition on 2016-04-28 at about $5.8B upfront, described Rova-T as a multi-billion-dollar peak-revenue opportunity and cited 44% ORR in DLL3-high relapsed SCLC from early studies. TAHOE enrollment was halted on 2018-12-05 because overall survival was shorter with Rova-T than topotecan. AbbVie then recorded a large Stemcentrx-related impairment, and on 2019-08-29 terminated the Rova-T R&D program after MERU showed no survival benefit at interim analysis.
possible_primary_source_types: AbbVie acquisition press release and SEC transaction filing
source_origin_notes: AbbVie press releases and AbbVie SEC filings are the same corporate origin for expectation/transaction claims, even when SEC gives stronger legal/accounting precision.
TAHOE and MERU registry records are sponsor-submitted registry material; use them for design/identifier history, not as an independent vote.
Accounting impairment amounts vary by gross/pre-tax/after-tax and contingent-consideration framing; preserve claim scope rather than forcing one number.

what_counts_as_support: Contemporaneous acquisition materials preserving AbbVie's expected commercial/clinical thesis before randomized failure.
TAHOE source documenting worse OS versus topotecan and the exact state change from active development to halted enrollment.
MERU/program-termination source documenting final R&D stop and no survival benefit.
SEC source linking clinical failure to impairment with accounting-scope precision.
what_counts_as_contradiction: Evidence that AbbVie did not materially base the acquisition thesis on Rova-T or did not communicate multi-billion-dollar expectations.
A later randomized study showing a clinically meaningful benefit that caused the program to resume before termination.
Evidence that impairment timing was driven by unrelated Stemcentrx assets rather than Rova-T probability changes.
unresolved_questions: What exact information was publicly known between the early 44% ORR narrative and AbbVie's 2018 decision not to seek accelerated approval?
Which impairment figure is appropriate for each claim: carrying-value write-down, pre-tax impairment, after-tax net impact, or contingent-consideration adjustment?
Can analyst/investor expectations at acquisition time be recovered without hindsight contamination?
delegated_evidence_instructions: Archive the 2016 acquisition announcement/filing, early Rova-T data source, 2018 accelerated-approval/TAHOE state changes, 2019 impairment filing and MERU termination. Build a point-in-time expectation trajectory: acquisition thesis -> accumulating uncertainty -> randomized harm/failure -> impairment -> termination. Preserve accounting measures as separate assertions.
